text:
Yuki: quick FYI - nightingale-q4-int4 canary showing a class of funcall failures I haven't seen before: base64 blobs in tool args get split across slice boundaries and then decoder fails (not a JSON parse error per se).
Marco: whoa. base64 in tool args? where is that coming from?
Yuki: we embed binary payloads (thumbnails, small attachments) as base64 inside the tool result for legacy tooling. typical payload: {\"tool\":\"image.attach\",\"args\":{\"b64\":\"SGVsbG8g...base64...\"}}
Deepti: paste a repro snippet?
Yuki: snippet from stream assembler logs: 
```
INVOKE id=bb204 model=nightingale-q4 slice=21/48
OUT >> {"tool":"image.attach","args":{"b64":"SGVsbG8gV29ybGQhAAAB..."}
...<slice ends>...
---next slice---
INVOKE continue id=bb204 slice=22/48
OUT >> "b64":"3Jk9...rest_of_blob=="}}
decoder: base64.DecodeError: invalid padding
```
Marco: so assembler concatenated strings but the cut happened inside the base64 chunk, producing invalid padding or broken 4-char groups. JSON itself might still be syntactically valid if assembler glued correctly, but decoder fails.
Deepti: right. this is subtly different from brace/brace split. Even a single-token tokenization shift can break the base64 4-byte alignment.
infra-bot: canary metrics: baseline base64-decode failures ~0.02% -> canary 0.9% (n=2200). top root cause: slice mid-base64 (87% of those failures). link: https://redwood.internal/canary/1788889999
Yuki: quick mitigations I can try today: (a) change encoder to use url-safe base64 with padding marker and a trailing sentinel, (b) switch to length-prefixed chunks (i.e., include a top-level `len` in args and stream raw bytes in chunked attachments), (c) runtime tactic: avoid cutting inside long string tokens by increasing slice margin for sequences with long string literals.
Marco: length-prefix sounds robust: assembler can reconstitute by concat and verify len before decode. overhead minimal and no need to change model tokenization.
Deepti: another option: at the assembler layer, when we detect a suspected base64 field (heuristic: long string of base64 charset and length > 256), we can delay parsing until we receive next slice and attempt to repair by reassembling and re-decode. cheap heuristic but race-y.
Yuki: propose micro-plan:
1) land a length-prefixed attachment proto in runtime (flag) so models can emit `"b64_len":1234, "b64_chunk":"..."` and assembler validates length before decode.
2) enable the assembler heuristic as a stopgap (detect long base64-like strings and buffer next slice)
3) instrument telemetry: `b64:heuristic_buffered`, `b64:length_pref_ok`, `b64:decode_repaired`
4) run 2h micro-canary with length-pref off (control) then on for 10% traffic.
Marco: agree. also run tokenizer diff fp16 vs int4 on a corpus that contains embedded base64 strings (weird edge-case often ignored) to measure how often token boundaries land inside long 4-char base64 groups.
Deepti: I'll add a tiny parser assertion to detect base64 padding errors and attach the raw slices to a debug bucket so we can analyze exactly where the cut lands.
infra-bot: created ticket RF-9461 and collector `s3://canary-dumps/nq4-b64-samples/` with automatic upload when padding error occurs.
eval-bot: aggregate: current canary b64-decode failure 0.9% -> target <0.05% after length-pref. will run sampling and post results.
Yuki: any objections to length-pref proto? it's a small change to the output schema for image.attach but backwards compatible if assembler tolerates missing len.
Marco: none. Deepti please prototype assembler len-check and buffering fallback. I can do the runtime flag.
Deepti: will prototype today and aim to enable the heuristic for the canary by tomorrow morning. will paste a few raw failed payloads here as we get them.
Yuki: thanks — keeping this thread as the single place for payload dumps and micro-canary results. :sparkles:
